subject: human skeleton
title: What If Your Bones Never Broke? A Connecticut Family Has That Gene

scenes.text: What if your bones never broke? One family in Connecticut carries the gene for it.
Doctors at Yale heard about an extended family with strangely dense bones. Twenty relatives gave blood. Seven had extremely high bone density.
None had any history of fractures. One researcher called them about the strongest bones on the planet.
The downsides were small: a deep, wide jaw, a bony growth in the mouth, and trouble staying afloat when swimming.
In 2002 the team traced it to one gene. A different mutation in that same gene does the opposite, and thins the bones.
The researchers saw a target: a medicine that copies this mutation could strengthen weak bones.

description:
What if your skeleton were almost unbreakable? In 2002, Yale researchers described an extended Connecticut family with extremely dense bones and no history of fractures. Of 20 relatives tested, 7 had the trait.
The cause was a mutation in the gene LRP5. Affected relatives had a deep, wide jaw, a bony growth on the palate and trouble staying afloat, but no symptoms. A different, function-losing mutation in the same gene causes low bone density, which made the pathway a target for osteoporosis drugs. The study appeared in the New England Journal of Medicine.
